Guides

Website for tradespeople: get found and receive requests

Your customers no longer flick through the directory. They type “plumber” and their town on their phone, then call one of the first results. Here is how to be one of them.

Why a tradesperson needs a website

Word of mouth still works, but it has changed. When a neighbour gives your name, the person looks you up on Google before calling. If they find nothing, or an old page with no photos, they hesitate.

A tradesperson’s website does three things: reassure people who already have your name, get you found by people who do not know you, and sort requests so you only keep the jobs that interest you.

What your website really must have

  • Your trade and your area, written out in full: “electrician in Sedan and 30 km around”. Google reads these words, and so do your customers.
  • Your services, one by one: repairs, renovation, new builds, maintenance.
  • Photos of your jobs, before and after. Three real photos are worth more than a nice stock image.
  • A simple way to reach you: a call button visible on phones and a quote form.
  • Your guarantees: ten-year liability insurance, qualifications, years in the trade.

Never make up customer reviews. A fake review is quickly spotted and destroys trust in one go. Instead, ask your recent customers to leave a real one on your Google profile.

One page or several?

If you do one trade in one area, the one-page website at €250 is enough to start: everything fits on one screen you scroll through.

If you have several activities (for example plumbing, heating and bathrooms), go for the showcase website at €350. Each activity has its own page, and each one can show up on Google for its own search. That is what brings the most requests over time. The guide one-page website or showcase website explains this choice in detail.

And while you are on the job?

You do not have time to look after a website, and that is normal. With a plan, hosting, the domain name and updates are handled for you. A photo to add, a price to change? You write it from your phone in your client area, and it is done by Lia straight away or by me within 72 hours.

The winning pair: website and Google profile

For a tradesperson, the website does not work alone. Your Google Business Profile puts you on the map when someone searches near them. It is free, and it links to your website.

Your questions

How much does a website for a tradesperson cost?

With me, €250 for a one-page website and €350 for a showcase website, at a fixed price. You pay 25% when you order and the rest when the website is live. After that, a plan from €5 a month covers hosting, the domain name and updates.

I have no photos of my jobs, what can I do?

Start with what you have, even two or three photos taken on your phone. Then get into the habit of photographing each job before and after: you send them to me, and the website grows over the months.

Does a website replace lead generation platforms?

Not necessarily straight away, but it makes you less dependent on them. On your website, the request comes straight to you, with no commission and without being compared with competitors on the same page.
